title: Hyperspectral Image Fusion with Spectral-Band and Fusion-Scale Agnosticism
claim: Existing methods are rigid, needing one model per configuration, isolated small data, and fixed scale; ours is one universal, joint-trained, arbitrary-scale model.
layout: 3 stacked panels, each left red existing vs right blue ours
description: Three horizontal gray panels stack vertically, each contrasting existing practice on the left in red and orange with our approach on the right in blue. Panel 1, Architectural Rigidity, shows three orange 3D cubes with 31, 103 and 191 bands, each feeding its own Model 1, 2 or 3. On the right the same blue cubes feed one gray Universal Model, which fans out to three output cubes. Panel 2, Data Scarcity Dilemma, shows three isolated small red datasets A, B and C on the left. On the right they sit inside a large teal circle labeled Combined Data, around a stack of blue slabs. Panel 3, Fixed Spatial Scale, shows grids passing through boxes trained for 2x scale, with a question mark for a 4x query. On the right a Continuous Representation box outputs 2x, 3.2x and 4x grids. Bold captions sit below each side, and the red versus blue color coding draws the eye first.
caption: Existing paradigms v.s. our universal approach for hyperspectral image fusion. Our method can suit different spectral bands joint training and can inference on arbitrary-scale fusion.
abstract: Current deep learning models for Multispectral and Hyperspectral Image Fusion (MS/HS fusion) are typically designed for fixed spectral bands and spatial scales, which limits their transferability across diverse sensors. To address this, we propose SSA, a universal framework for MS/HS fusion with spectral-band and fusion-scale agnosticism. Specifically, we introduce Matryoshka Kernel (MK), a novel operator that enables a single model to adapt to arbitrary numbers of spectral channels. Meanwhile, we build SSA upon an Implicit Neural Representation (INR) backbone that models the HS signal as a continuous function, enabling reconstruction at arbitrary spatial resolutions. Together, these two forms of agnosticism enable a single MS/HS fusion model that generalizes effectively to unseen sensors and spatial scales. Extensive experiments demonstrate that our single model achieves state-of-the-art performance while generalizing well to unseen sensors and scales, paving the way toward future HS foundation models.
